population: Crohn's disease patients vs. matched non-IBD controls
source: Manceur AM, Ding Z, Muser E, et al. Burden of Crohn's disease in the United States: long-term healthcare and work-loss related costs. J Med Econ. 2020;23(10):1092-1101.
note: Work-loss (absenteeism) costs PPPY: $5,490 in the CD cohort vs. $3,322 in the matched non-IBD cohort ($2,168 increment, p<.001). Retrospective claims-cohort analysis, OptumHealth Care Solutions Inc., Jan 1 1999 - Mar 31 2017, average 5-year follow-up, 1:5 matching. Absenteeism imputed from claims data; presenteeism (on-the-job productivity loss while working) was NOT assessed, so this figure is itself a floor, not a full societal-cost estimate. Not stratified by disease activity/health state -- this is a population-average increment over the whole follow-up window (a mix of active-disease and remission periods for real patients), applied in this project as a flat per-living-cycle cost identical across all non-Death health states and all arms (UST/IFX/ADA/CT/Treg alike), since no more granular breakdown is available in the source. Whether Treg's own Sustained Deep Remission (cured) state should be exempted from this cost, paralleling the SDR-utility argument (analysis_plan.md sec 6.2, S7), is a stated, undecided modelling choice -- not resolved by this row.
